Situation1: They join in when the family talks about possible weekend plans.
Expectation2: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation2: A friend on their way to the airport calls, thinking they left their passport at home, and asks if you can check and bring it to them right away.
Story: As I sat at the dinner table, my family’s laughter filled the room. We were tossing around ideas for the weekend—maybe a hike, maybe a movie night. My younger sister looked at me, her eyes bright, waiting for my input. I knew how much these moments meant to everyone, especially after a busy week. Just as I was about to suggest a picnic, my phone buzzed. It was Sam, my closest friend. His voice was frantic—he was already halfway to the airport and thought he’d left his passport at home. He begged me to check his place and, if it was there, rush it to him. I could hear the panic in his voice, and I knew how important this trip was for him. My family, meanwhile, was still waiting for me to join in, to be present, to help decide our plans. I felt torn, the weight of both expectations pressing down on me, my mind racing as I tried to figure out what to do.
